title: Is AI Impacting Global Labor Markets? - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. As companies integrate artificial intelligence (AI) tools into their operations, the effects on hiring are starting to show up in the economic data for some industries and workers around the world, according to Goldman Sachs Research. The timing and extent of AI’s impact on job markets depend on the rate of adoption among companies. However, there are inconsistencies in surveys about AI adoption, leading to results that often vary widely. To overcome this, our economists compiled 11 different surveys that measure AI adoption across countries and applied a statistical algorithm to extract rankings, write Goldman Sachs Research economist Sarah Dong and Joseph Briggs, who leads the Global Economics team, in a report. After rescaling around the OECD’s adoption survey­—the most globally comprehensive measure in our economists’ compiled data—Goldman Sachs Research finds that major developed markets are ahead of other countries in deploying AI, with adoption rates between 15%–20%. Among developed markets, France, the US, the Netherlands, and the UK score at the top end of this range of AI adoption. In major emerging markets, adoption rates are in the range of 10%–15%, according to Goldman Sachs Research estimates. Our economists also find that industries with greater exposure to AI automation have been associated with slower growth in job openings since the second half of 2022. The relationship between exposure to AI and slower growth in job openings was more pronounced in Germany, Australia, and the US. “This cross-industry result confirms our prior finding that the onset of generative AI tools may have led companies in highly exposed industries to re-evaluate their hiring plans,” Dong and Briggs write. There is evidence that employment in information and communication services, two of the industries that are the most exposed to AI, has slowed because of AI, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Employment in these sectors has slowed across nearly all major developed markets since 2022. In the US, employment in those industries has fallen below its long-run trend, while it remains near or above the long-run trend in other developed countries. “These patterns suggest tech sector (broadly defined) hiring headwinds are global in nature, although outright negative impacts are most compelling in the US,” Dong and Briggs write. Beyond information and communication services, an assessment of other industries with high exposure to AI reveals a similar, albeit more muted, pattern of AI-related employment headwinds relative to the US. Employment in call centers, software publishing, management consulting, and advertising services has fallen sharply below trend across the developed world. Call center employment, for instance, now stands 39% below trend in the US, 33% below trend in Canada, and 27% below trend in Germany. “These patterns confirm that, like in the US, AI-employment headwinds are visible in industries where labor-automating tools are already available,” Dong and Briggs write. Goldman Sachs Research performed another analysis, which included AI-exposure scores in a cross-country panel for more than 800 occupations, to more rigorously test the impact of AI on employment. Our economists find that a 10% occupational exposure to AI is only associated with a 0.1 percentage point drag to annual headcount growth in France, Canada, and the US. The analysis suggests that “economy-wide hiring headwinds remain limited,” Dong and Briggs write. While AI’s overall impact on job markets appears limited, recent anecdotes and US labor market data suggest that AI displacement could be stronger among entry-level workers. Goldman Sachs Research’s analysis of occupational growth based on entry- and non-entry-level groups signals that junior workers may face greater headwinds to hiring due to AI adoption. “AI-related hiring headwinds are clearly visible in official and unofficial employment data, but impacts are limited to a narrow set of industries and workers,” Dong and Briggs write. title: The National Police Association Endorses the Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act - National Police Association
content:
INDIANAPOLIS, September 3, 2026 — The National Police Association (NPA) endorses the Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act (H.R. 10070), introduced by Rep. Andy Barr (KY-06) and co-sponsored by Rep. John McGuire (VA-05). This bill expands special overtime pay to U.S. Border Patrol agents at every General Schedule (GS) grade. Under current law, only GS-12 Border Patrol agents receive special overtime pay: an additional 50% of the hourly rate of basic pay for regularly scheduled overtime hours under the Border Patrol Agent Pay Reform Act. That payment is in addition to the 25% overtime supplement lower grades already receive for a scheduled 10-hour workday. The Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act removes the GS-12 restriction, extending the extra 50% overtime payment to agents at all levels. The 25% overtime supplement would remain. It has been referred to the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee; the text for the bill is here. Regardless of service level, Border Patrol agents work long hours in remote and harsh conditions. The dangers and risks they routinely confront, including being targeted by criminal organizations, aren’t limited to a single pay grade. “Border Patrol agents are dedicated public servants committed to the same mission of keeping our borders safe. They should receive consistent overtime pay,” said Paula Fitzsimmons, Legislative Director, National Police Association. Though U.S. Customs and Border Protection has reported increased hiring numbers and a record agent headcount, the agency remains short of its stated force goal of 25,000 agents. Compounding this is an approaching retirement wave that will strain staffing if hiring and retention do not keep pace. “Expanding the special overtime pay benefit to all Border Patrol agents will aid in recruiting, while improving morale and retention among current agents,” Fitzsimmons added. A related Rep. Barr bill called the Border Patrol Supervisors Retention Act (H.R. 8956) introduced earlier this year, would extend the same special overtime to agents at GS-13 through GS-15, who are likewise currently ineligible. The NPA commends Reps. Barr and McGuire for introducing the Border Patrol Overtime Parity Act and urges Congress to pass it. title: The Adventure Bike With Honda Reliability And Triumph Sophistication - HotCars
content: Subscribe to the HotCars newsletter to never miss an update Motorcycles are often fair weather friends. They are great fun on that perfect sunny Sunday morning, but when times get tough that two-wheeled companion can stay locked up in the nice cozy garage. But not adventure bikes. These motorcycles are designed to do everything from blasting across a desert to hacking through a jungle — there is very little that an adventure bike isn't prepared for. We've updated this article with more details on how this bike stacks up against its rivals and a closer look at the different versions available. With a range of accessories, rugged capability, and a comfortable riding position, this is the type of bike that you can rely on when the going gets tough. But there is one that perfectly blends upmarket sophistication with dependable reliability, plus a backstory that begins in one of the world's toughest endurance races. This is one bike you can use on more than just Sunday... Adventure motorcycles, or ADV bikes, are designed to be the Swiss army knives of two-wheeled ownership. These bikes are equally at home on almost any terrain, whether you are traversing the Sahara or riding to Siberia. Of course, a lot of people just use them for regular daily riding, and maybe the odd weekend away, but that's OK. With a comfortable seating position and typically large displacement engines, they soak up the miles on asphalt too. Adventure bikes can trace their history back to scramblers and dirt bikes, with Yamaha bringing the concept to the streets in 1968 with the pioneering DT-1, an off-road machine that could be ridden easily on the streets. By the early '80s, events like the Paris-Dakar race were capturing the public's imagination, and with the rise of backpacking as an alternative to commercial package holidays, bikers realized that motorcycles could take them on adventures they never before dreamed possible. At the forefront of the adventure bike movement was German brand     BMW. While superbikes were all the rage in 1980, BMW decided to buck the trend at the IFMA international show in Cologne. The Bavarian brand unveiled the R80 G/S, a new type of motorbike that was something of a mash-up of every kind of bike you could imagine—the first adventure motorcycle, in fact. It had a capable flat-twin airhead engine, matched to knobby tires, two-up space, and the upright comfort of a tourer. The G/S in the name stood for Gelände/Straße, or "off-road/street" in Teutonic parlance. In 1981, Frenchman Hubert Auriol won the Paris-Dakar Rallye piloting a BMW R 80 G/S, proving the bike's off-road capabilities. Auriol repeated his victory in 1983, while in 1984 and 1985, Belgian Gaston Rahier also won onboard a BMW. In 2018, BMW introduced the new BMW R 1250 GS as the latest in its line of adventure bikes. The Bavarian company has a long history of creating bikes that eat up the miles, and this was designed to be one of the most accomplished. The R 1250 GS features a vastly improved boxer engine with BMW ShiftCam Technology for variation of valve timing and valve stroke on the intake side, with increased power across the entire power band. The 1,254cc powerplant is good for 136 hp at 7,750 rpm and 105 lb-ft of torque at 6,500 rpm. The motor also features asynchronous valve opening on the intake side for improved air-fuel mixture and better effective combustion, along with a knock sensor system to allow for use of variable fuel quality while on the move. The camshaft drive is via toothed chain, replacing a roller chain, and BMW fitted a new exhaust system (with closed-loop catalytic converter technology) for better performance. The oil supply has been improved, and the bike is fitted with the latest generation of BMS-O engine control. As well as taking on the established tech and dependability of the Japanese brands, BMW has also pitched the R 1250 GS against upmarket Triumph. The British brand is known for combining high-tech and sophistication with old-school looks. While the GS doesn't go down the classic styling route, it has plenty of upmarket sophistication that will appeal to the well-heeled Triumph crowd. The GS has connectivity as standard, with a multifunctional instrument cluster that features a large 6.5-inch full-color TFT display. This is supplemented with an analog speedometer and tachometer. These bikes come with two ride modes as standard: ASC (Automatic Stability Control) and Hill Start Control. “Dynamic Traction Control” (DTC), "Dynamic Pro", "Enduro" and "Enduro Pro" ride modes are available as an option. Optional Dynamic ESA means that the bike automatically adapts to riding conditions and movements, as well as providing automatic ride height adjustment. Finally, the BMW Motorrad Spezial has a range of customization features available as factory options. Triumph offers standard factory customization as well as the Triumph Factory Custom (TFC) with ultra-premium options that are often hand-finished. BMW has made its name on a blend of quality and performance, and it seems that the R 1250 GS fits into that. Owners at Advrider.com say there have been some minor issues, but these have reportedly been ironed out, and the bikes have clocked up big mileages. One owner on a Facebook discussion said: "I bought a 2023 R1250 GS Trophy model. Last year of the 1250 GS version. BMW had pretty much completely debugged the model by then. No issues so far." As the bike is so new, it shouldn't cause too many problems, especially if you go for a full service history from an authorized BMW dealership. These bikes are known for clocking up a lot of miles due to the fact they make for good do-it-all machines. As another option, the Honda Africa Twin is seen as the gold standard among the company's adventure bikes. The 2026 model, which employs Honda’s 1,084cc parallel-twin engine, is highly dependable and reliable. The BMW R 1250 GS comes in two flavors, and they target different types of adventure riders. The standard GS is the easier-going option, with a 20-liter tank, adjustable seat, 6.5-inch TFT, boxer engine, shaft drive, and BMW's sophisticated electronic rider aids. For riders who want a more agile machine for daily commuting, tight trails, and weekend touring, the standard bike makes a compelling case. It's lighter at 549 pounds ready to ride, carries a lower seat than the GSA, and is easier to manage at parking-lot speeds. And when things go sideways off-road, there's less motorcycle to wrestle back onto its wheels. Then there's the R 1250 GS Adventure. The GSA adds a huge 30-liter tank, taller suspension, and additional body and engine protection, making it better suited to cross-continent trips, remote terrain, and cold-weather touring. Its taller seat and larger physical footprint also make it a natural choice for tall or larger riders who want extra legroom and a commanding riding position. The BMW R 1250 GS may be the benchmark in big-bore adventure bikes, but there's no shortage of challengers waiting to steal its crown. Triumph comes closest with the Tiger 1200, a direct GS rival that combines a 147-hp inline-three with the same low-maintenance shaft-drive layout. The Triumph has 11 more horsepower than the BMW, but the GS counters with a muscular 105 lb-ft of torque and a more relaxed, low-revving character. For sheer firepower, Ducati and KTM turn the dial way up. The     Multistrada V4 S makes 170 hp, while KTM's 1290 Super Adventure S delivers 160 hp. But peak power isn't the whole story. The BMW's 105 lb-ft of torque actually tops both, beating the Ducati's 92 lb-ft and edging the KTM's 102 lb-ft. The Ducati and KTM also rely on chain final drives that require more routine attention than the BMW's shaft. Honda takes the more dirt-focused route with the Africa Twin Adventure Sports, using its 1,084cc parallel-twin to favor smooth, predictable performance over outright acceleration. Ultimately, each rival has a specialty, but the GS remains the consummate all-rounder, blending strong performance, touring prowess, road manners, off-road capability, sophisticated electronics, and shaft-drive convenience. A 2008 Honda Civic Si will cost on average $15,283, says Classic.com, but for this kind of money you can get a BMW R 1250 GS that is just a few years old. Scouring the classifieds brought up some surprising results. The R 1250 GS cost $22,615 in 2019, but prices are much lower now. On Bringatrailer.com, we found a 2020 bike with 5,000 miles and a BMW-branded top box and side cases that had sold for $15,750. A 2019 bike with 24,000 miles was naturally more affordable, costing just $11,200. The bottom line is that you will need around $15,000, it seems, to get the keys to one of these capable adventure bikes on the used market. As with any used purchase, it's important to do your homework and not be tempted by very low prices, but the R 1250 GS offers a lot of can-do attitude for the money. We want to hear from you. title: Meet U of G’s First Schulich Leaders - U of G News
content: Canada’s largest undergraduate STEM scholarships support entrepreneurial-minded students Learning how to put AI to use for the greater good and helping Canadian farmers with food sustainability are the goals of two Schulich Leaders who will begin their journeys at the University of Guelph this fall. Aryan Thakur will pursue computer engineering and Matteo Volpini will study agriculture with the support of Schulich Leader Scholarships, Canada’s most prestigious STEM scholarship program. Schulich Leader Scholarships provide $100,000 for a science, technology or math degree, or $120,000 for an engineering degree, for entrepreneurial-minded students. U of G is proud to be part of the prestigious scholarship program as it’s a testament to the University’s ability to attract some of Canada’s most competitive STEM students who aspire to careers in tech, engineering and applied research. “As we celebrate 15 years of Schulich Leaders, we are proud to have supported more than 1,000 exceptional Canadian students pursuing STEM degrees at our country’s top universities,” says Judy Schulich, president, The Schulich Foundation. “Schulich Leader Scholarships help attract and retain outstanding talent, empowering the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs. By supporting their ambition and creating the conditions for them to succeed, we can ensure their innovations drive Canada’s future prosperity.” A Schulich Leader Scholarship is life changing, says Aryan Thakur, whose interest in artificial intelligence and machine learning drew him to U of G’s Computer Engineering program in the College of Engineering. As part of a generation who grew up alongside technology, Thakur knew early on he wanted to be part of an industry revolutionizing the world. “AI and machine learning are going to provide a lot of opportunity,” he says, “and I want to align myself with that.” Eager to launch his own start-up, Thakur says his program’s co-op stream is the kind of experiential learning that will build a foundation for him, from which to grow his own ideas. He knows there is work to do in the field. AI is not yet functioning at 100%, and so he is dedicated to being part of improving it, ultimately putting it to use for good. “I want to help people,” he says, “using technology to have a meaningful impact.” Being a Schulich Leader is about more than just financial support, he says. “The ability to network with fellow Scholars really does help with job opportunities or even just aligning with others going through the same life transition.” It was while growing up on a small hobby farm learning tree pruning and how to pick cherries and peaches and apples that Matteo Volpini learned the kind of devastation disease can bring to plants and the crops of farmers. The years his family lost nearly 200 trees to disease, pests and the environment, he started researching where he could study plant science and food sustainability. What he found was the Bachelor of Science in Agriculture program at the Ontario Agricultural College. “I’m excited to learn more about gene-editing technology, gain more plant knowledge and learn how disease affects plants, how pesticides and fungicides can help prevent these things,” he says. His goals don’t end there. “I’d like to start a business dedicated to global food sustainability that supports Canadian farmers by developing resilient crop varieties that can better withstand environmental stressors like pests, disease and unpredictable weather.” As a Schulich Leader, he joins a community of STEM students with similar interests across a broad spectrum of disciplines. “It’s such a great resource to have,” he says. “There are so many opportunities to learn from each other or to collaborate.” Recognizing the increasing importance and impact that STEM disciplines have on the prosperity of future generations, businessman and philanthropist Seymour Schulich established this $200 million scholarship fund in 2012 to encourage our best and brightest students to become Schulich Leader Scholars: the next generation of entrepreneurial-minded, technology innovators. Through The Schulich Foundation and United Jewish Appeal, these prestigious entrance scholarships are awarded to 100 high school graduates enrolling in a science, technology, engineering or mathematics (STEM) undergraduate program at 20 partner universities in Canada. Every high school in Canada can submit one Schulich Leader Nominee per academic year based entrepreneurial leadership and financial need.

We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. NEW YORK, NY, September 2, 2026 – The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS) today announced that it will redeem all of the issued and outstanding 1.542% Fixed/Floating Rate Notes due September 10, 2027 (the “ Fixed/Floating Rate Notes”) on September 10, 2026 (the “Fixed/Floating Rate Notes Redemption Date”) and all of the issued and outstanding Floating Rate Notes due September 10, 2027 (the “Floating Rate Notes” and, together with the Fixed/Floating Rate Notes, the “Notes”) on September 10, 2026 (the “Floating Rate Notes Redemption Date” and, together with the Fixed/Floating Rate Notes Redemption Date, each a “Redemption Date”). The Fixed/Floating Rate Notes have an aggregate principal amount outstanding of $2,750,000,000, and the Floating Rate Notes have an aggregate principal amount outstanding of $300,000,000. Each series of Notes will be redeemed for a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount of such series of Notes plus accrued and unpaid interest to but excluding the applicable Redemption Date for such series of Notes (each a “Redemption Payment”, and together, the “Redemption Payments”). From and after the applicable Redemption Date for such series of Notes, all interest will cease to accrue on such series of the Notes. Investors in the Notes should contact the bank or broker through which they hold a beneficial interest in the Notes for information about obtaining the Redemption Payment for any Notes in which they have a beneficial interest. Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE: GS) and a consortium of 21 global banks plan to launch a USD stablecoin by 2027. The bank-led consortium aims to issue a regulated, USD-backed digital token distinct from any central bank digital currency. The group intends to use the stablecoin for cross-border payments, institutional settlements, and broader digital asset market activity. Plans include potential future expansion into additional fiat currencies through the same shared infrastructure. Its global banking relationships and transaction infrastructure are central to how this stablecoin project could be integrated into real world financial flows. Beyond the headline: 2 risks and 3 things going right for Goldman Sachs Group that every investor should see. For investors, this stablecoin push is less about a new crypto token and more about how Goldman Sachs extends its existing strengths in payments, trading, and balance sheet management. The consortium structure spreads build out costs and regulatory work across 21 banks. That can reduce execution risk for Goldman while still giving it a seat at the table in how large scale tokenised settlement evolves. It also aligns with the firm's activity in issuing multiple senior and callable notes across different maturities, which shows ongoing attention to funding and liability structure that could support future digital asset infrastructure spend. The practical test is whether large clients start using the consortium's USD token at scale once it goes live.
